correctness.rationale: For every off-branch A of finite (member-dependent) chain height, r_A(x)=the maximum length of a chain ending at x is defined; if x is a proper prefix of y then r_A(x)<r_A(y). Thus the finitely many rank levels partition A into antichains. Keeping all infinite levels preserves pairwise almost-disjointness. For any infinite antichain C, C is off-branch, so maximality of O supplies an A with |C∩A| infinite; finite rank pigeonhole gives a level with infinite C-intersection, proving the new antichain family maximal. Each A contributes finitely many levels, and |O| is infinite by the known lower bound for the off-branch invariant; |B|<=|O| follows. Contraposition proves that if o<bar{o}, every o-sized maximal family contains at least one member with chains of arbitrarily large finite length. This does not show any infinite branch contained in a member, nor resolve the consistency problem.
residual_risks: The conditional premise o<bar{o} may be undecidable; the argument does not establish it.
An off-branch set may have unbounded finite chain height but meet every branch only finitely.
